title: Baby and Bridal Shower Planning Kit
subtitle: Everything a host needs to plan a baby or bridal shower: who hosts, timeline, games, food amounts, budget, and thank-you tracking.
intro: A shower is a few hours of warmth, good food, and a little silliness for someone you love. This kit helps you divide the work, build a timeline, plan the menu, and keep track of every gift and thank-you note. It works for baby showers, bridal showers, and couples showers alike.

sections.heading: Who Hosts and Who Pays
items: Traditionally, close friends or family host the shower, not the guest of honor. Many hosts now share the work and the cost.
For a bridal shower, the maid of honor and bridesmaids often host, with help from the mothers or grandmothers.
For a baby shower, a sister, best friend, coworker, or grandparent often hosts. A co-host group is common.
Agree on a total budget before anyone buys anything, and put each host's contribution in writing.
Split jobs by strength: one host handles invitations, one handles food, one handles decor, one handles games.
Check with the guest of honor about the guest list, theme, and any off-limits topics before you plan.
Ask the guest of honor's family for key names and addresses, but let the guest of honor approve the final list.
Include co-workers, neighbors, and extended family only if the guest of honor wants them there.
Decide early whether partners and kids are invited, and say so clearly on the invitation.
For a surprise shower, appoint one person as the decoy to get the guest of honor to the venue.

sections.heading: Shower Timeline
sections.note: Most showers happen 4 to 8 weeks before the wedding or 4 to 8 weeks before the due date. Spring and early summer weekends fill up fast in the Chicago area.

tasks: Choose the date with the guest of honor and key guests in mind.
Set the budget and decide who is hosting.
Draft the guest list and get addresses.
Pick a venue: home, restaurant, brunch spot, garden, or rented hall.
Choose a theme and color palette.
Check the registry and decide on a gift expectation, such as books for the baby or recipes for the bride.
Send invitations by mail or email with an RSVP date.
Include the registry details and any dress code.
Reserve rentals: tables, chairs, linens, plates, glassware, and a tent if outdoors.
Book the caterer, baker, or order from a local restaurant.
Hire a photographer for an hour or assign a friend.
Plan games and activities and order any supplies.
Order decor: banners, balloons, flowers, and signs.
Plan the menu and drinks, including non-alcoholic options.
Order or make favors.
Arrange for a gift table and a place to store gifts.
Follow up on RSVPs.
Give the final headcount to the caterer and rental company.
Prepare the gift-tracking sheet and thank-you list.
Plan the seating, including a special chair for the guest of honor.
Create a playlist.
Confirm the weather plan for outdoor showers.
Confirm deliveries and vendor arrival times.
Buy non-perishable food and supplies.
Print games, signs, and name tags.
Assign helpers: greeters, gift recorders, photographers, cleanup crew.
Prepare a small thank-you note kit with pens and cards.
Set up tables, chairs, and decor.
Prepare make-ahead dishes and chill beverages.
Receive and inspect rental deliveries.
Set out food, games, and gifts table before guests arrive.
Welcome guests with a drink and a name tag.
Take photos of the guest of honor with each guest.
Count and load gifts in the guest of honor's car.
Return or arrange pickup of rentals.
Pay vendors and send tips.
Send the gift-tracking sheet to the guest of honor.
Send guests a thank-you message and photos.
Remind the guest of honor to send thank-you notes within a month or two.

groups.title: Invitations and guests
items: Confirm the guest list with the guest of honor.
Include the date, time, address, RSVP, and host contact on the invitation.
Add registry details and any theme or dress code.
Note whether the shower is for women only, a couples shower, or open to all.
Send a reminder text to guests a few days before.
Plan accessible seating and parking for older guests.

groups.title: Venue and setup
items: Reserve the venue and confirm the setup time.
Arrange tables for dining, gifts, desserts, and games.
Set up a photo backdrop or corner.
Create a welcome sign and signage for food stations.
Place decorations at eye level and at the entrance.
Put out seating for older guests and plenty of napkins.

groups.title: Rental items
items: Order one chair per guest plus a few extras.
Choose table sizes: 60 in rounds for seated lunch, 6 ft rectangles for buffets.
Order linens that match the theme.
Rent plates, flatware, glasses, and serving pieces to cut down on waste.
Add a drink dispenser or beverage tub.
Rent a tent and heaters or fans for outdoor showers.

groups.title: Day-of supplies
items: Scissors, tape, and a trash bag for gift wrap.
Gift recorder pad and pens.
Camera or phone charger.
Extra napkins, wet wipes, and a first aid kit.
Tissues for happy tears.
Containers for leftovers.

sections.heading: Games and Activities
sections.note: Choose two or three. Many guests prefer fewer games and more conversation.

groups.title: Baby shower
items: Guess the baby food flavors.
Baby bingo while the guest of honor opens gifts.
Advice cards and wishes for the baby.
Guess the due date or birth weight.
Decorate onesies with fabric markers.
Diaper-raffle ticket with each gift of diapers or wipes.
Book instead of a card: each guest signs a book for baby's first library.

groups.title: Bridal shower
items: How well do you know the bride trivia.
Recipe cards for the couple's first meals.
Memory jar with stories and advice.
Wedding dress paper craft or toilet-paper veil contest.
Mimosa bar or tea tasting.
Scavenger hunt in the venue.
Candle or flower arranging as a group activity.

groups.title: Both
items: Guest book or photo wall.
Photo booth with props.
Word-scramble or word-search with themed words.
Door prizes for the winners.
Slideshow of the guest of honor through the years.
A group toast.

sections.heading: Menu Amounts
sections.note: For a 2 to 3 hour brunch or lunch shower. Increase if serving a full dinner. Amounts are rough planning numbers.

sections.heading: Shower Budget Split
sections.note: A rough guide for a seated brunch or lunch shower. Costs vary a lot across Chicago and the suburbs.

lines.tip: Hosting at home can save most of this line, but you may still need tables, chairs, and linens.
Brunch is often less expensive than dinner. Order desserts from a local baker.
Choose a few high-impact items rather than many small ones.
Digital invitations are fine for most showers.
Small prizes work well. Use items the guests will actually use.
Edible or plant favors are well-loved and easy to pack.
Ask a friend, or hire a photographer for one hour.
Set this aside for extra guests, weather changes, or forgotten items.

sections.heading: Gift-Opening and Thank-You Tracker
sections.note: Make several copies. Record each gift as it is opened so thank-you notes are quick and personal.
fields: Gifts needing a separate thank-you for a group gift
